title: A choice-free construction of a leafless balanced subtree

standard_prerequisites.name: ZF set theory without the axiom of choice
standard_prerequisites.statement: Recursion on the natural numbers, separation, finite unions of finite sets, and stabilization of a decreasing sequence of nonempty subsets of a fixed finite set are allowed.
standard_prerequisites.use: Form definable pruned trees and their intersection. No countable sequence of independently chosen successors is available.

standard_prerequisites.name: One fixed explicit repetition schedule
standard_prerequisites.statement: There is an explicit sequence of natural numbers in which every natural number occurs infinitely often, for example concatenating the finite strings (0), (0,1), (0,1,2), and so on.
standard_prerequisites.use: Revisit every level after changes above it, without making choices in the input tree.

core_obligations: At each scheduled level, identify all nodes with an infinite upward subtree and retain all those having the least current degree, without choosing a distinguished node or successor.
Show each pruning leaves a downward-closed tree with infinitely many finite nonempty levels, although it can change degrees at earlier levels.
Use repeated visits rather than a single pass so changes at every fixed level and its successor level eventually stabilize.
Prove that the intersection has a nonempty set on every level, no leaves, and equal successor counts within each level, all in ZF.

proof_roadmap.step: Define a fixed recurrent schedule and prune by the definable class of infinite-tail nodes having minimum degree at the scheduled level.
For each fixed level, the decreasing finite node sets stabilize; revisit the level after its own and the next level node sets have stabilized to obtain the final common positive degree.

difficulty_reason: The target is a uniform ZF existence theorem for trees whose finite levels need not admit a simultaneous ordering. A branch-by-branch or one-pass degree selection would invoke countable choice and does not prove it. The author uses recurrent global pruning with a minimum-degree/infinite-tail invariant and a two-level finite stabilization argument to overcome that obstruction. Independent review should judge this actual choice-free construction; the proof length and set-theory terminology alone do not certify H2.

compared.difference: The old primary classifies equivalence of FM atom sets from densely ordered weakly2-transitive trees. This task is a ZF pruning construction on height-omega trees with finite levels; no FM-model classification or dense-tree code is used.

editorial_notes: The ambient theory is ZF without the axiom of choice, following the author convention69-74. A bare appeal to the infinite-branch form of Konig lemma for arbitrarily labelled finite levels would assume the very choice principle that this proof avoids.
The sequence of trees is defined by a fixed numerical schedule and by whole definable node classes; the construction does not select one member from each level.

For the last sentence of source513, use stabilization of both level n and level n+1, then a subsequent visit to level n. The sets of surviving successors and therefore their degrees are then the final ones. This spells out the author stated finite-stabilization argument; it does not add another construction.

editorial_scope: One choice-free subtree theorem. The finite levels are not assumed collectively well-orderable, and no infinite branch is asserted. Fraenkel-Mostowski models, dense weakly2-transitive trees and the paper later template classification are outside the counted proof.

source_authorship.known_AI_disclosure: No AI-assistance declaration located in the read author/abstract/end matter and selected proof; no assertion about undisclosed tools.

review_checkpoints: All X_n are nonempty because a finite level covers the infinite tail by finitely many upward subtrees, so at least one such subtree is infinite. The least degree is a natural-number minimum, and all minimizers are retained.
Intersection nonemptiness uses nested subsets of one fixed finite level, which requires no choice axiom. The proof does not infer an infinite branch.
Equal degree at a finite stage can later fail after pruning higher levels; the recurrent schedule and stabilization of two consecutive levels are essential.
Difficulty must be assessed without allowing countable choice or the arbitrary finite-level Konig lemma; allowing those would trivialize the intended mathematical issue.

issues_for_independent_review.detail: Assess whether the recurrent pruning and no-choice invariant together meet H2; if viewed as a routine exercise under the stated ZF prerequisites, hold it rather than inheriting H2 from the paper topic.

disposition.reason: Independent reviewer confirms proof complete and choice-free but judges the remaining pruning/stabilization argument below H2 under the allowed inputs.
